| Scene description | • The site is public space in Donghu Jingyuan Residential Community, Hongshan District.<br>• S01-B-01: a red-and-white cylindrical waste bin at the roadside pavement edge has orange and other peel on its lid and a little nearby litter; it is annotated as overflowing.<br>• S01-B-02: a clean stainless-steel recyclables/other-waste bin stands in a square before steps without spillage.<br>• S01-B-03: three wooden planters line the path. The left planter contains obvious accumulated waste and is annotated as overflowing; the other two contain no obvious waste and are annotated as non-overflowing.<br>• S01-B-04: a green other-waste/recyclables bin beside stairs on a brick path does not spill; a black waste bag is visible at the opening. Some stains, leaves, and peel occur on the ground, without extensive accumulation. |
| Regulatory basis | • Residential public areas require standard sorting containers kept clean and free of overflow; property or managing organizations are responsible for maintenance and collection (Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 12).<br>• Managers should collect regularly to prevent overloaded or overflowing bins and scattering (Implementation Plan for the Municipal Solid Waste Classification System, State Council General Office Document [2017] No. 26, Article 5).<br>• Ground around bins and public containers should remain clean, without accumulation or stains (Standard for the Provision of Urban Environmental Sanitation Facilities, CJJ 27-2012, Section 5.2.3).<br>• Littering in public areas is prohibited; residents should use designated containers (Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 30).<br>• Managers should remove overflow or accumulation within 24 hours of discovery; otherwise warnings or fines may apply under Article 36 of the same Regulations, with CNY 500–2,000 for serious cases. |
| Severity | **Moderate.** Two overflows and one accumulation are reported. Although pollution is not extensive, spillage and scattered waste impair residential sanitation and indicate inadequate public-container management, requiring prompt intervention. |
| Impact assessment | Visible impacts: overflow and scattered peel and stains impair pedestrian access and the visual environment. Possible short-term impacts: delayed removal may attract flies and mosquitoes, support bacterial growth and disease transmission, prompt complaints, and reduce community satisfaction. |
| Potential causes | - **Possible cause 1:** insufficient or delayed collection. Overflow at S01-B-01 and S01-B-03 suggests this; the planter at S01-B-03 is nonstandard and may be excluded from routine collection.<br>- **Possible cause 2:** improper disposal. Peel on the lid and ground litter at S01-B-01 suggest littering or disposal without proper lid closure.<br>- **Possible cause 3:** unsuitable provision or capacity. A nonstandard planter at S01-B-03 serves as a waste container and readily overflows.<br>- **Verification:** review collection records and bin plans and observe disposal behavior and use frequency. |
| Long-term effects | If persistent or recurrent, accumulation may become routine, increasing insects and odors and impairing community health. It may also reduce willingness to sort waste, undermine management credibility, and diminish residential environmental quality. |
| Recommendations | - **Immediate actions:** clear overflow and scattered litter at S01-B-01 and S01-B-03; assess the planters' purpose and remove them or add warnings if they are not waste containers; inspect bin lids and ensure no spillage.<br>- **Long-term measures:** improve collection frequency in heavily used areas; clarify the purpose of nonstandard containers such as planters to prevent misuse; strengthen sorting education and disposal guidance; inspect routinely to identify and address overflow and accumulation early. |
| Priority | **Medium.** The problem is not a major pollution or public health emergency, but spillage and ground contamination affect residents and pose sanitation risks. Removal and initial rectification are needed within 24 hours to prevent deterioration. |
